node.label: Raymond Williams
node.date_label: 1958: Culture and Society, 1780–1950 · 1976: Keywords: A Vocabulary of Culture and Society · 1989: The Politics of Modernism (posthumous; edited and introduced by Tony Pinkney)
node.description: A Welsh cultural historian, critic and novelist whose historical research on culture and society informed cultural materialism. He joins ordinary ways of life to artistic creation, while criticizing both restricted cultural privilege and prescriptions that would dictate socialist art in advance.

proposed_edges.relationship: Joins culture as ordinary social meanings and ways of life with artistic learning and creative work.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own Culture Is Ordinary, pp. 92–94 read; the essay’s conjunction is preserved instead of reducing culture either to elite arts or to an undifferentiated way of life.

proposed_edges.relationship: Criticizes a prescriptive Marxist account that would dictate cultural meanings and artistic forms from a proposed system of production.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own essay pp. 95–96 read. He retains the importance of production and restricted educational access while rejecting directive cultural prescriptions; this is criticism within his engagement with Marxism, not rejection of all materialist historical analysis.
